activePlacements.alt: Imagined scene: An oil flask, myrrh and pale blossoms rest beside a window overlooking vineyards.

textChecked.kjv: Because of the savour of thy good ointments thy name is as ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.
textChecked.web: Your oils have a pleasing fragrance. Your name is oil poured out, therefore the virgins love you.

textChecked.kjv: Look not upon me, because I am black, because the sun hath looked upon me: my mother's children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; but mine own vineyard have I not kept.
textChecked.web: Don’t stare at me because I am dark, because the sun has scorched me. My mother’s sons were angry with me. They made me keeper of the vineyards. I haven’t kept my own vineyard.

textChecked.kjv: While the king sitteth at his table, my spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof.
textChecked.web: While the king sat at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.

textChecked.kjv: A bundle of myrrh is my well-beloved unto me; he shall lie all night betwixt my breasts.
textChecked.web: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh, that lies between my breasts.

textChecked.kjv: My beloved is unto me as a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of Engedi.
textChecked.web: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms from the vineyards of En Gedi.

textChecked.kjv: The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing of birds is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;
textChecked.web: The flowers appear on the earth. The time of the singing has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.

textChecked.web: By night on my bed, I sought him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.

textChecked.kjv: I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
textChecked.web: I will get up now, and go about the city; in the streets and in the squares I will seek him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.

textChecked.web: My sister, my bride, is a locked up garden; a locked up spring, a sealed fountain.

textChecked.kjv: Thy plants are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; camphire, with spikenard,
textChecked.web: Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates, with precious fruits, henna with spikenard plants,

textChecked.kjv: Spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:
textChecked.web: spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of incense tree; myrrh and aloes, with all the best spices,

textChecked.web: a fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, flowing streams from Lebanon.

textChecked.kjv: Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.

activePlacements.alt: Imagined scene: A wooden door and simple latch catch soft light on a dewy night.

textChecked.kjv: I sleep, but my heart waketh: it is the voice of my beloved that knocketh, saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night.
textChecked.web: I was asleep, but my heart was awake. It is the voice of my beloved who knocks: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; for my head is filled with dew, and my hair with the dampness of the night.”

textChecked.kjv: I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?
textChecked.web: I have taken off my robe. Indeed, must I put it on? I have washed my feet. Indeed, must I soil them?

textChecked.kjv: My beloved put in his hand by the hole of the door, and my bowels were moved for him.
textChecked.web: My beloved thrust his hand in through the latch opening. My heart pounded for him.

textChecked.kjv: I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers with sweet smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.
textChecked.web: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the handles of the lock.

textChecked.kjv: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone: my soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.
textChecked.web: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved left, and had gone away. My heart went out when he spoke. I looked for him, but I didn’t find him. I called him, but he didn’t answer.

activePlacements.review: Dewy stone, wooden door, latch and nighttime light fit the doorway sequence. No person, detached hand or modern lock is invented. Door fastening is illustrative, not a precise reconstruction of the ancient mechanism.
